test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 21 Jun, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Two trains, A and B started travelling towards each other at the same time, from places P to Q and Q to P, respectively. After crossing each other, A and B took 9 hours and 16 hours to reach Q and P, respectively. If the speed of A was 56 km/h, then what was the speed (in km/h) of B?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of train A = 56 km/h.

Time taken by train A to reach Q after crossing train B = 9 hours.

Time taken by train B to reach P after crossing train A = 16 hours.

**Formulae Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

For the same distance, we can write

{S1 over S2} = sqrt{T2over T1}

where S1, S2, and T1, T2 are the respective speeds and times of the objects.

**Calculation:**

S1 be the speed of A

{56 over S2} = sqrt{16over 9}

 

S2 = 42 km/hr

the speed (in km/h) of B = 42 km/hr
